newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends up, helped by speculators and NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends up, helped by speculators and NY.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures closed higher across the board on Tuesday, boosted by speculative buying and a technical breakthrough by New York futures.
May coffee ended up $25 at $1,578 per tonne and July rose $30 to $1,592. Volume was heavier than recent days, tallying 5,674 lots.
CSCE July coffee's breakout to the upside on Monday from a narrowing triangular formation was seen as constructive for coffee, in general.
That breakout got positive reinforcement when May followed suit, traders said. CSCE futures have been benefitting from a squeeze on the May contract there before its first notice day on April 22.
May open interest in New York fell 852 contracts to 8,439 as of Monday's close.
Those upside breakouts encouraged some speculative and fund buying in both New York and London in the afternoon, traders said. They also noted some trade buying.
However, gains were capped here by scaled-up origin sales.
July resistance was pegged at a gap between $1,611 and $1,620. Support rests at $1,546.
Earlier in the day, May/July switches dominated as investors rolled nearby positions.
News of a lower Colombian crop estimate and an indefinite strike at Brazil's key port of Santos also supported prices.
Later on Tuesday, the U.S. Green Coffee Association will report March stock data.
